events.label: dynasty_start
events.text: First Taungoo dynasty period begins, per the 1485–1599 range.

events.label: founding
events.text: Mingyi Nyo founds the First Taungoo dynasty at Taungoo.

evidence.quote: towards the end of the Ava Kingdom in 1510

events.text: Tabinshwehti crowned king of all Burma at Bagan.

evidence.quote: In 1544 , Tabinshwehti was crowned as king of all Burma at the ancient capital of Bagan

events.label: war
events.text: Burmese–Siamese War begins; Tabinshwehti defeated at Ayutthaya.

events.label: war
events.text: Burmese–Siamese War ends, per the 1547–49 range.
Tabinshwehti assassinated, ending his reign.
Bayinnaung succeeds Tabinshwehti to the throne.

evidence.quote: Bayinnaung , succeeded to the throne in 1550

events.label: campaign
events.text: Bayinnaung invades Manipur.

events.label: campaign
events.text: Bayinnaung invades Ayutthaya.
Bayinnaung dies, ending his reign.

events.label: founding
events.text: Toungoo rulers found a second, Restored dynasty at Ava.

evidence.quote: founded a second dynasty at Ava , the Nyaungyan or Restored Taungoo Dynasty ( 1597–1752 )

events.label: dynasty_end
events.text: First Taungoo dynasty ends, per the 1485–1599 range.
Anaukpetlun, Bayinnaung's grandson, begins his reign.

events.label: military
events.text: Anaukpetlun reunites Burma and defeats Portuguese attempts.
Anaukpetlun's reign ends, per the 1605–1628 range.
Thalun succeeds as king and rebuilds the war-torn country.

events.label: reform
events.text: Burmese crown begins comprehensive censuses, consolidating provincial manpower and taxes.

evidence.quote: Beginning in 1635 , the Burmese crown began to conduct comprehensive censuses

events.text: Thalun's reign ends, per the 1629–1648 range.

events.label: rebellion
events.text: Mon rebellion in Lower Burma began, founding the Restored Hanthawaddy Kingdom

evidence.quote: In 1740 , the Mon people in Lower Burma began a rebellion , founding the Restored Hanthawaddy Kingdom

events.label: dynasty_end
events.text: Hanthawaddy armies capture Inwa, ending the Toungoo dynasty.

evidence.quote: captured Inwa in 1752 and ended the 266-year-old Toungoo dynasty

events.text: Mahadhammayaza dies, ending the dynasty's survival.

evidence.quote: until the death of Mahadhammayaza in 1752

undated_mentions: mid-16th century: Toungoo dynasty begins ruling Burma
1720s: Meitei raids begin on the kingdom
1730s: Meitei raids intensify, reaching central Burma
Tabinshwehti moves capital to Bago for commercial strategic position
Tabinshwehti crushes the Hanthawaddy capital of Bago
Bago rebels against Inwa, encouraged by the French
Restored Toungoo kings based at Ava (Inwa)
